result.topic_en: Case III of Euler's theory of fluid friction: water flowing out of a constantly full vessel through a horizontal pipe, with the height due to the efflux velocity, the special case of a very wide vessel, and the condition for water to actually flow out.
result.transcription:
DE FRICTIONE FLVIDORVM. 367
CASVS III.
SI AQVA EX VASE CONSTANTER PLENO
PER TVBVM HORIZONTALEM
EFFLVIT.
76. Sit vafis amplitudo $AA = ff$, et altitudo $AB = a$, tubi vero horizontaliter infixi longitudo $BC = b$, amplitudo $BB = gg$, et lumen, per quod aqua effluit, $CC = kk$. Ponatur breuitatis ergo $\mathfrak{A} = e^{\frac{-\alpha a}{f}}$; $A = \frac{1-\mathfrak{A}}{\alpha}$; $\mathfrak{B} = e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}}$; $B = \frac{1-\mathfrak{B}}{\alpha}$; $\mathfrak{f} = \frac{k^4}{f^4}$; et $\mathfrak{g} = \frac{k^4}{g^4}$; erit altitudo celeritati effluxus debita, ob $\zeta = 90^\circ$, et cof. $\zeta = 0$, denotante $l$ altitudinem 30 pedum,
$$v = \frac{A\mathfrak{B}f - (1-\mathfrak{A}\mathfrak{B})l}{1-\mathfrak{B}\mathfrak{f}-\alpha B\mathfrak{g}}$$
77. Si vas $AB$ fuerit valde amplum, erit $\mathfrak{f} = 0$, $\mathfrak{A} = 1 - \frac{\alpha a}{f}$ et $A = \frac{a}{f} - \frac{\alpha aa}{2ff}$, vnde celeritas effluxus debita erit altitudini
$$v = \frac{a\mathfrak{B}(1-\frac{\alpha a}{2f}) - (1-\mathfrak{B}+\frac{\alpha a}{f}\mathfrak{B})l}{1-(1-\mathfrak{B})\mathfrak{g}}$$
vnde cum $\mathfrak{g} = \frac{k^4}{g^4}$ vnitatem fuperare nequeat, denominator femper erit quantitas affirmatiua $> \mathfrak{B}\mathfrak{g}$: quod indicio eft, aquae effluxum certo ad ftatum vniformitatis peruenire.
78. Vt autem aqua actu effluat, neceffe eft, vt fit $a\mathfrak{B}(1-\frac{\alpha a}{2f}) > (1-\mathfrak{B}+\frac{\alpha a}{f}\mathfrak{B})l$, feu
$\mathfrak{B} > \frac{fl}{f(a+l)-\alpha a(\frac{1}{2}a+l)}$; ideoque $e^{\frac{\alpha b}{g}} < 1 + \frac{a}{l}$
$- \frac{\alpha aa}{2fl}$

items.quote: vnde cum $\mathfrak{g} = \frac{k^4}{g^4}$ vnitatem fuperare nequeat, denominator femper erit quantitas affirmatiua $> \mathfrak{B}\mathfrak{g}$: quod indicio eft, aquae effluxum certo ad ftatum vniformitatis peruenire.
items.english: Hence, since g = k^4/g^4 cannot exceed unity, the denominator will always be a positive quantity greater than Bg, which indicates that the efflux of water certainly reaches a state of uniformity.

items.quote: Vt autem aqua actu effluat, neceffe eft, vt fit $a\mathfrak{B}(1-\frac{\alpha a}{2f}) > (1-\mathfrak{B}+\frac{\alpha a}{f}\mathfrak{B})l$
items.english: For the water actually to flow out, it is necessary that aB(1 - αa/2f) > (1 - B + (αa/f)B)l, i.e. that B exceeds fl/(f(a+l) - αa(a/2 + l)), and hence that e^{αb/g} be less than 1 + a/l - αaa/(2fl) ... (the expression continues on the next page).
